text: C3a opens: read AGENT.md, the head, the stage file, diary --last 5, validate.py --open C3 (0 errors, 0 warnings), the PI's message (J: 'what matters is that you build something you believe in, and you did'; rulings stand, QC2-001 and QC2-002 included). Then prior.md read whole before anything else, as section 1 asks. Next: METHOD.md's first section and the shelves already held, then the read-log counts, then the shelf.

Re-read before the shelf (stage C3 section 1): METHOD.md's first section, Suddaby (2006) whole, Gioia, Corley and Hamilton (2013) whole. Next: Grodal, Anteby and Holm (2021), Eisenhardt (1989), Langley (1999), Van de Ven and Poole (1990), then the read-log counts.

Re-read before the shelf: Grodal, Anteby and Holm (2021) and Eisenhardt (1989) whole. Eisenhardt's enfolding step (conflicting literature first, then similar) is this stage's first two legs. Next: Langley (1999), Van de Ven and Poole (1990).

Re-read before the shelf: Langley (1999) whole; page 12 (lines 959 to 1767) is Figure 2 extracted as noise, read to line 1440 and checked by pattern to 1767 for words (none). Next: Van de Ven and Poole (1990).

notes-C3.md opened: the literature is read after the model (the design, no departures line); the substitution held in names (no tier named for the four problems; the words appear only in two changed sentences), and its cuts are C3c's test; prior.md quoted and set against the model; the method shelf re-read whole; the log point recorded: _cite_reads-C3.jsonl 0 lines (absent), _mem_reads-C3.jsonl 63 lines, before any explanation-shelf work is served.

Explanation shelf, read whole (verified): Puranam, Alexy and Reitzig (2014). Its claims that bear here: a form of organizing is a set of solutions to four universal problems, individually necessary and collectively sufficient (p. 166); goalless networks and crowds are ruled out (p. 164); self-selection, transparent task division, intrinsic reward and virtual collaboration are complements (pp. 173-174); visible work simplifies coordination (p. 172); authority in open source is the right to accept or reject contributions and membership (p. 173). First reading: it is the standing claim for C3c, and it resembles more than it contradicts (visible work, a host's right to accept guests). Next: Felin and Zenger (2017).

Explanation shelf, read whole (verified): Felin and Zenger (2017). Claims that bear here: economic actors' theories (questions, problems, contrarian beliefs) direct perception and reveal value (pp. 260-263); organizations grant some actors' theories power, aid their composition, and attract those who share the theory by self-selection (p. 265); hierarchy decides when discussion does not (Simon, quoted p. 265). First reading: a candidate contradiction on what settles what a room acts on (a chosen theory against the topic's given picture), and a resemblance in self-selection to a starter's proposal. Next: Felin and Zenger (2016).

Explanation shelf, read whole (verified): Felin and Zenger (2016, SSRN manuscript pages). Claims that bear here: a firm's theory reveals an architecture and bundle of problems to solve, and guides which to solve itself and which to leave to others (pp. 4-5, 11); serendipitous need-solution pairs are others' priced solutions (p. 8); even recognizing a solution needs a theory (p. 14). First reading: with the 2017 paper, a candidate contradiction on what settles a room's work; the room's goal (a picture) is mostly given, not composed as a contrarian theory. Next: O'Mahony and Ferraro (2007).

Explanation shelf, read whole (verified): O'Mahony and Ferraro (2007). Claims that bear here: 'Before an organization can develop a form of governance, it must establish a shared basis of authority' (p. 1081); Debian ran five years on de facto founder rule, recalled an autocratic second leader, then wrote a constitution with positional authority limited by democratic means (pp. 1088-1090); members came to elect organization builders, and face-to-face ties predicted the leadership team (pp. 1091, 1098). First reading: a contradiction with the model's claim that rooms organized almost without decided order; the likely resolution is the setting (73 hours against 13 years), to be decided from the record. Next: Bechky (2006).

Explanation shelf, read whole (verified): Bechky (2006). Claims that bear here: temporary organizations are not ephemeral but 'organized around structured role systems whose nuances are negotiated in situ' (p. 3); the generalized role structure travels by interorganizational careers, and film sets are temporary total institutions (pp. 8-10); roles are enacted by enthusiastic thanking, polite admonishing and role-oriented joking (pp. 11-13); she asks 'how temporary organizing can be successful in settings without a generalized role structure' (p. 17). First reading: a contradiction about what coordinates a temporary group (a carried role structure against calls and a visible work), likely resolved as a difference of setting the paper itself names; the enactment practices resemble the rooms' credit and refusals. Next: March (1991).

Explanation shelf, read whole (verified): March (1991), read last and weighted below the others. Claims that bear here: an organizational code that newcomers learn and that learns from them (mutual learning, pp. 74-75); slow socialization and moderate turnover keep the diversity the code learns from, 'the development of knowledge may depend on maintaining an influx of the naive and ignorant' (p. 86); exploitation crowds out exploration (p. 73). First reading: no contradiction with the model; a resemblance for C3b on newcomers and the host sub's code. All six works of the read tier are read. Next: the contradictions, with the model's statements on roles and decided order.

Abductive read, prompted by O'Mahony and Ferraro (2007): a production community establishes a shared basis of authority before it can govern itself (p. 1081), and the canvas-born factions at the far end of the decided-order claim's range look like that. What it makes me look for: whether decided order (rooms placed on Decided order) gathers in rooms that rule on other rooms' works (hosts vetting guests' requests, T3-162; colour factions, Neo-tribes T4-023) more than in other rooms, held to room size by items_in_window quartile with a permutation null within quartile (seed 20261014), counted with mem.py rooms --with over the 705 analysed rooms; then quotes through cite.py from the rooms that show it. A rooms --with T4-011 call with --limit 5 was run before this line to see the output format; it served four room names.

Move (relating or contrasting), abductive, prompted by O'Mahony and Ferraro (2007): F-006 (decided order is rare) superseded by a bounded line, and a C01 history line written (abductive, prompted_by). Decided order gathers in rooms placed on a colour-faction theme or on vetting guests' requests: 7 of 39 (0.179) against 39 of 666 (0.059); held to size 7 against a null mean of 2.7 (p95 5, p 0.014); the gap is in the two smaller size quartiles (5 of 14 against 13 of 339) and vanishes in the two larger (2 of 25 against 26 of 327); 0 of 56 rooms that asked a host for space. The disagreement is about the setting (73 hours and one picture against 13 years and one code base) and bounds the claim. findings.jsonl 21 lines, history.jsonl 83. Snapped C3-move-relating-48. Also seen, not acted on: PurplePixels c0165 calls a member 'a fellow comrade during the button', a tie from an earlier event, which bears on the colour-faction boundary.

literature-C3.md written (Leg 1: O'Mahony and Ferraro, setting, bounds both, F-006 bounded; Bechky, setting, bounds hers, her own open question on settings without a role structure; Felin and Zenger, different things, the goal question left to C3c; Olson recalled, open; Puranam and March read and not taken as contradictions; one abductive read; no switch record). manifest-C3.txt written (no stage C3 successor yet). validate.py C3: 0 errors, 0 warnings after rewording a manifest line that named a file not yet written. Contradictions: O'Mahony and Ferraro (2007), setting, bounds both, one abductive read bounded F-006 (decided order gathers in small canvas-born colour factions, 7 of 39 against 39 of 666, held to size p 0.014); Bechky (2006), setting, bounds hers; Felin and Zenger (2016, 2017), different things, the goal question to C3c; Olson (1965, recalled), open. Puranam and March not contradictions. No switch record; no arrow, element statement, tier or concept changed; snap C3-move-relating-48.
